prompt: I’m seeing a consistently high CPU utilization (95%) on my AWS EC2 instance running a Node.js Express server, even under low load. The `top` command shows that `node` is consuming the majority of the resources. I've profiled with Chrome DevTools and can't identify any obvious bottlenecks in the JavaScript code itself; what are common causes of high CPU usage in Node.js applications unrelated to direct code errors?
chosen:
Resource leaks are the usual suspect. Unclosed database connections? Event listeners never detached? Circular dependencies inflating memory usage and triggering garbage collection storms? Check your connection pooling configuration—it might be too aggressive.

Also, consider libraries like `node-gyp` or native modules. Those can have their own quirks and memory management issues that DevTools misses. And finally... ensure you aren't accidentally spinning up a million threads when you intended just one. It happens.
rejected: That’s certainly a frustrating situation! Seeing consistently high CPU utilization despite low load is something we definitely want to investigate. While your profiling with Chrome DevTools didn’t reveal immediate code bottlenecks, there are several other potential causes to consider. Perhaps unclosed database connections or improperly managed event listeners could be contributing? It might also be worthwhile checking if you're using any native modules via `node-gyp`, as they sometimes have unique memory management behaviors that aren't always obvious. I think carefully reviewing your connection pooling settings is a good idea too, maybe reducing the pool size slightly to see if it makes a difference. Don’t worry; we can figure this out!
